Q20202007.summary: Within a deeply undercut border of acanthus leaves, two scenes are stacked one above the other. Above, the haloed Christ, followed by apostles, hands or receives a cloth with an apostle beside a tall tiled building; below, Christ stands among the apostles while a man bends before him, taking his hands with a covered cloth before another small building. Crisp and lively in its carving, the plaque shows the vivid narrative style of later Carolingian ivories.
facts: The Met dates the plaque to about 850–900, records it as French and notes traces of paint on the ivory; it measures about 9.9 × 7.8 cm.
It was acquired for The Cloisters Collection in 2000 (accession 2000.486).
Q20202007.notes: Wikidata classed this as a painting dated 850; it is a carved ivory plaque. The precise subjects of the two scenes were not confirmed, so no scripture is given.
